title: Paperwork: taxes and a performance review
subtitle: Documenti, tasse e lavoro
intro: Tax season: a T4 arrives, a free tax clinic at the Lillian H. Smith library, a Notice of Assessment in impeccable officialese. At the bakery, Chiara's first performance review with Priya, and a letter from Doug for her immigration file. This unit builds the English [[relative clauses]] (defining vs non-defining, who/which/that/whose/where, zero relative), the formal register ([[Dear Sir / Madam]], [[I am writing with regard to]], [[I would be grateful if]]), [[so that / in order to]], and the modals of obligation in full ([[must / have to / need to / be required to / be supposed to]]).
objectives: Scrivere lettere ed email formali: [[I am writing with regard to]], [[I would be grateful if you could]], [[Please find attached]], [[Yours faithfully]]
Capire documenti ufficiali: T4, Notice of Assessment, CRA letters, Record of Employment
Usare le frasi relative: [[the clinic that offered free help]], [[the woman who helped me]], [[the office where I filed]], [[the manager whose office is on the second floor]]
Scrivere e capire frasi di finalità: [[in order to apply]], [[so that we can process your file]]
Padroneggiare i modali dell'obbligo: [[must / have to / need to / be required to / be supposed to]]
canDo: B1 · Reading: can understand a Canadian tax document and a formal letter.
B1 · Writing: can write a formal English email with the right register.
B1 · Spoken interaction: can participate in a performance review and ask for feedback.
B1 · Lexis: knows the vocabulary of Canadian taxes and employment basics.
B1 · Spoken production: can describe people and processes with precise relative clauses.

sections.title: T4, the tax clinic, and a performance review
sections.intro: Three scenes: the T4 arrives in February; a free tax clinic at the Lillian H. Smith library; a Friday performance review at the bakery. Listen for relative clauses (which, who, whose, where), formal register, and the full set of obligation modals.

blocks.title: The T4 arrives
blocks.setting: Thursday 25 February, 6 p.m., Chiara's basement kitchen. Sofia at the table, Chiara with a sealed envelope that just arrived from Doug's. On the table: a tax guide, a laptop open to the CRA website, two glasses of wine.
blocks.register: informal between flatmates, with the formal document in the middle

lines.t: The T4 just came. Doug mailed it. — You've got until April 30 to file. Open it. — Line 14, employment income: $34,760. Line 22, income tax deducted: $5,891. Line 18, EI premiums: $594. Line 16, CPP contributions: $1,744. Numbers I didn't know had names.
lines.n: È appena arrivato il T4. L'ha mandato Doug. — Hai tempo fino al 30 aprile per fare la dichiarazione. Aprilo. — Riga 14, reddito da lavoro: 34.760 dollari. Riga 22, imposta trattenuta: 5.891. Riga 18, premi EI: 594. Riga 16, contributi CPP: 1.744. Numeri che non sapevo avessero nomi.
lines.note: The T4 is the Canadian equivalent of the Italian CUD / Certificazione Unica. The CRA (Canada Revenue Agency) is the tax authority. EI (Employment Insurance), CPP (Canada Pension Plan).

lines.t: I'll help you. The free tax clinic at the Lillian H. Smith library — the one that's on Toronto Public Library's clinic page — opens at 2 p.m. tomorrow. Volunteers who are trained by the CRA help with simple returns. Our incomes are low enough. We go together.
lines.n: Ti aiuto io. La clinica fiscale gratuita alla biblioteca Lillian H. Smith — quella che è nella pagina delle cliniche della Toronto Public Library — apre alle 14 domani. I volontari addestrati dalla CRA aiutano con dichiarazioni semplici. I nostri redditi sono abbastanza bassi. Andiamo insieme.
lines.note: The one that's on the Library's page: defining relative clause with that. Volunteers who are trained by the CRA: non-defining or defining relative with who. The CVITP (Community Volunteer Income Tax Program): free help for Canadians with low income.

lines.t: I'll bring my T4, my SIN card, my RRSP contribution slip from the bakery, which Doug sent me last week, and the rent receipts, which the landlord gives me every month. — Add the TTC bill, which can be deducted for low-income earners.
lines.n: Porto il T4, la tessera SIN, lo RRSP contribution slip dalla panetteria, che Doug mi ha mandato la settimana scorsa, e le ricevute dell'affitto, che il proprietario mi dà ogni mese. — Aggiungi la bolletta TTC, che si può detrarre per i redditi bassi.
lines.note: Four non-defining relative clauses with which (which Doug sent, which the landlord gives, which can be deducted). Note the comma before each which.

lines.t: Who processes it after? — Volunteers at the clinic do the data entry; a tax preparer who's certified by the CRA reviews it; then it's filed through CRA My Account, which uses NETFILE. Thirty minutes if the forms are simple. The Notice of Assessment arrives in two to eight weeks, with your refund or your balance owing.
lines.n: Chi la lavora dopo? — I volontari fanno l'inserimento; un preparatore certificato dalla CRA la rivede; poi è trasmessa via CRA My Account, che usa NETFILE. Trenta minuti se i moduli sono semplici. L'avviso di accertamento arriva in due-otto settimane, con il tuo rimborso o il saldo da pagare.
lines.note: A tax preparer who's certified: defining relative. CRA My Account, which uses NETFILE: non-defining with which. The whole Canadian tax-process vocabulary in four lines.

lines.t: Will I get a refund? — With your income and your rent, almost certainly. Not big — 400 or 500 dollars. Also: you need to apply for the GST/HST credit, which is extra money every three months for low-income earners. — I need to apply for everything I'm entitled to.
lines.n: Avrò un rimborso? — Con il tuo reddito e il tuo affitto, quasi sicuramente. Non grande — 400 o 500 dollari. Inoltre, devi fare domanda per il credito GST/HST, che è denaro extra ogni tre mesi per i redditi bassi. — Devo fare domanda per tutto a cui ho diritto.
lines.note: The GST/HST credit, which is: non-defining. Everything I'm entitled to: zero relative pronoun (that I'm entitled to) + preposition at the end.

notes.phrase: the clinic that's on the page · a tax preparer who's certified · the slip, which Doug sent · the rent receipts, which the landlord gives me · the TTC bill, which can be deducted · the GST/HST credit, which is extra money
notes.note: Six relative clauses. Defining (no comma) vs non-defining (with comma). Which for things (non-defining), who for people (defining or non-defining), that in defining only.

notes.phrase: T4 · CRA · SIN · RRSP · EI · CPP · NETFILE · CRA My Account · Notice of Assessment · refund · balance owing · GST/HST credit
notes.note: The Canadian tax vocabulary. These acronyms you learn once and use every April.

blocks.title: The Lillian H. Smith tax clinic
blocks.setting: Friday 26 February, 2:45 p.m., Lillian H. Smith branch of the Toronto Public Library on College Street. Sofia and Chiara at a desk with Prisca, a retired accountant who volunteers every Friday during tax season. Winter light through tall windows.
blocks.register: informal professional, between a volunteer and taxpayers

lines.t: Hello. Prisca Kim, I'm the volunteer who'll help you today. Have you brought your T4, your SIN card, and all other income slips? — Yes. — Good. Any dependents? Any disability? Any medical expenses over 3% of your income? Any charitable donations? Any union dues? Any tuition in the last ten years?
lines.n: Salve. Prisca Kim, sono la volontaria che vi aiuterà oggi. Avete portato il T4, la tessera SIN e tutti gli altri slip di reddito? — Sì. — Bene. Dipendenti? Disabilità? Spese mediche sopra il 3% del reddito? Donazioni? Quote sindacali? Tasse scolastiche negli ultimi dieci anni?
lines.note: The volunteer who'll help you: defining relative. The list of deduction categories: a mini-tour of the Canadian tax deductions.

lines.t: No dependents, no disability, no major medical, no donations, no union, no tuition in Canada. I paid tuition for a year of a master's in Italy in 2024, but that was in Italy; I don't think I can claim it. — Correct, you can't; that's an Italian certificate. What about moving expenses? When you came to Toronto in September 2024, were you offered employment?
lines.n: Nessun dipendente, nessuna disabilità, nulla di medico, nessuna donazione, nessun sindacato, nessuna tassa scolastica in Canada. Ho pagato un anno di master in Italia nel 2024, ma era in Italia; non credo di poterlo detrarre. — Giusto, no; è un certificato italiano. Spese di trasloco? Quando sei arrivata a Toronto a settembre 2024, ti era stato offerto un lavoro?
lines.note: Were you offered employment: past perfect passive, the formal register of the question. Moving expenses can be deducted if the move was for employment and you moved at least 40 km closer.

lines.t: I came on a Working Holiday permit without a job. I started at Doug's a month later. — Then no, moving expenses don't apply. Everything you brought is enough. Give me ten minutes, I'll do the data entry, and we'll NETFILE it together. — Thank you.
lines.n: Sono venuta con un permesso Working Holiday senza un lavoro. Ho iniziato da Doug un mese dopo. — Allora no, le spese di trasloco non si applicano. Tutto quello che hai portato è sufficiente. Dammi dieci minuti, faccio l'inserimento, e poi facciamo il NETFILE insieme. — Grazie.

lines.t: You're done. Your refund will be approximately $437. The Notice of Assessment will arrive in your CRA My Account inbox in two to eight weeks. Which is where you also claim your GST/HST credit — I ticked the box so that it's processed automatically. Keep this receipt for seven years, which is how long the CRA may audit you back.
lines.n: Fatto. Il rimborso sarà di circa 437 dollari. L'avviso di accertamento arriverà nella tua casella CRA My Account in due-otto settimane. Che è anche il posto dove richiedi il credito GST/HST — ho spuntato la casella perché venga lavorata in automatico. Tieni questa ricevuta per sette anni, che è quanto a lungo la CRA può controllarti indietro.
lines.note: The CRA My Account, which is where you claim: non-defining with where. So that it's processed automatically: so that + clause for purpose. Seven years, which is how long the CRA may audit you back: non-defining relative with the special pronoun how long.

notes.phrase: the volunteer who'll help you · the clinic that's on the page · the preparer who's certified · the slip which Doug sent · the inbox where you claim · the box so that it's processed · seven years which is how long
notes.note: A full spectrum of relative clauses in two scenes. Who / which / that / where / plus the zero relative (everything you brought).

notes.phrase: dependents · disability · medical expenses · charitable donations · union dues · tuition · moving expenses · deduction · credit · refund · NETFILE · the Notice of Assessment

blocks.title: Priya's office · the performance review
blocks.setting: Monday 1 March, 5:15 p.m. After the bakery closes. Doug's small back office. Priya at the desk with a two-page printed form. Chiara in a chair, nervous. A kettle whistling in the back.

lines.t: Sit down, Chiara. This is your first performance review. I'll be reviewing you, which is unusual because Doug is the owner, but he asked me to since you report to me. I have a two-page form that I need to go through with you. If there's anything you want to raise, add it at the end.
lines.n: Siediti, Chiara. Questo è il tuo primo colloquio di valutazione. Ti valuterò io, cosa inusuale perché Doug è il proprietario, ma mi ha chiesto di farlo visto che tu riporti a me. Ho un modulo di due pagine da scorrere con te. Se c'è qualcosa che vuoi sollevare, aggiungilo alla fine.
lines.note: Which is unusual because: non-defining relative modifying the whole previous clause. A two-page form that I need to go through with you: defining relative with that + preposition at the end.

lines.t: First, the positives. You have been with us for six months, which is the probation period at Doug's. In those six months you have grown from a dishwasher who could barely pronounce pasticciotto to a baker whose pasticciotti sell out every Saturday morning and whose attention to detail has improved our Instagram presence.
lines.n: Prima, i positivi. Sei con noi da sei mesi, che è il periodo di prova da Doug. In quei sei mesi sei passata da lavapiatti che a stento pronunciava pasticciotto a fornaia i cui pasticciotti vanno a ruba ogni sabato mattina e la cui attenzione ai dettagli ha migliorato la nostra presenza su Instagram.
lines.note: A dishwasher who could barely pronounce: defining relative with who. A baker whose pasticciotti sell out: whose + noun (= of whom). The relative pronoun of belonging.

lines.t: You bring values that we want to see here: punctuality, respect for ingredients, kindness to customers, the willingness to clean a floor at 7 a.m. and still smile. These are things that are hard to teach. — Thank you.
lines.n: Porti valori che vogliamo vedere qui: puntualità, rispetto per gli ingredienti, gentilezza con i clienti, la disponibilità a pulire il pavimento alle 7 di mattina e ancora sorridere. Sono cose che è difficile insegnare. — Grazie.
lines.note: Values that we want to see: defining relative. Things that are hard to teach: defining relative.

lines.t: Areas for improvement. You're supposed to track your inventory on the pastry board at the end of every shift, which you forget about once a week. You need to practise your English pronunciation of three words that keep tripping you up: pasteurised, hydrogenated, allergens. These are things that must be clear when you talk to a parent of a child with an allergy. — Noted.
lines.n: Aree di miglioramento. Dovresti registrare l'inventario sulla lavagna di pasticceria alla fine di ogni turno, cosa che dimentichi una volta a settimana. Devi esercitare la pronuncia inglese di tre parole che continuano a inciamparti: pasteurised, hydrogenated, allergens. Sono cose che devono essere chiare quando parli con un genitore di un bambino allergico. — Preso nota.
lines.note: You're supposed to track: be supposed to = expected to. You need to: necessity. These are things that must be clear: must as modal of obligation. Three overlapping modals of obligation (supposed to / need to / must).

lines.t: Doug and I are offering you a 1.25-dollar-an-hour raise, effective March 15, which brings you to $19.25 an hour, 20% above the Ontario minimum. In addition, Doug has written a letter of support for your immigration file, which I will give you in a sealed envelope at the end. You don't have to use it; it's yours if you want it.
lines.n: Doug e io ti offriamo un aumento di 1,25 dollari all'ora, dal 15 marzo, che ti porta a 19,25 dollari all'ora, 20% sopra il minimo dell'Ontario. Inoltre Doug ha scritto una lettera di supporto per la tua pratica d'immigrazione, che ti darò in busta chiusa alla fine. Non devi usarla; è tua se la vuoi.
lines.note: Which brings you to: non-defining. Which I will give you in a sealed envelope: non-defining. You don't have to use it: don't have to = no obligation (unit 12).

lines.t: I don't know what to say. — Say thank you and sign here. We're required to keep both your copy and ours. Your signature confirms you've read the review, not that you agree with every word.
lines.n: Non so cosa dire. — Dì grazie e firma qui. Siamo tenuti a conservare la tua copia e la nostra. La tua firma conferma che hai letto la valutazione, non che sei d'accordo con ogni parola.
lines.note: We're required to keep: passive obligation (be required to). Your signature confirms you've read… not that you agree: a two-part contrast.

notes.phrase: which is unusual · a form that I need to go through with you · a dishwasher who could barely · a baker whose pasticciotti sell out · values that we want to see · things that are hard to teach · which you forget about · three words that keep tripping you · which brings you to · which I will give you
notes.note: Ten relative clauses in one scene. Mix of defining (no comma, no which allowed) and non-defining (comma + which or who). Whose for both people and things in English (whose attention).

notes.phrase: you're supposed to · you need to · must be clear · we're required to keep · you don't have to use it · effective March 15 · letter of support · performance review · raise · probation period
notes.note: The modals of obligation and the vocabulary of a Canadian performance review.

questions.q: «The clinic that's on the Library's page» is a:
options: Defining relative clause (no comma; that is fine).
questions.why: Defining = essential to identify the noun. Non-defining = extra info, with commas, uses which (not that).

questions.q: «You're supposed to track inventory» means it's your expected duty, not an iron rule.
questions.why: Be supposed to = expected to. Softer than must or have to.

questions.q: The volunteer ___ (who/which) helped me was great. The receipt ___ (who/which) she gave me is in my file. The office ___ (who/which) handles tax is on CRA My Account.
questions.n: La volontaria che mi ha aiutata è stata bravissima. La ricevuta che mi ha dato è nel mio archivio. L'ufficio che gestisce la tassa è su CRA My Account.

sections.title: Taxes, work rights, formal English
sections.intro: Four themes: Canadian taxes vocabulary, labour rights and the Employment Standards Act, formal English, and the language of a performance review.

ex.t: You have until April 30 to file your tax return.
ex.n: Hai tempo fino al 30 aprile per fare la dichiarazione dei redditi.

items.note: File a tax return (verb). Also simply return. The individual version.

ex.t: The CRA processes 30 million tax returns a year.
ex.n: La CRA lavora 30 milioni di dichiarazioni l'anno.

items.note: The federal agency. ARC in French. Lives at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.

ex.t: Doug mailed my T4 at the end of February.
ex.n: Doug ha spedito il mio T4 a fine febbraio.

items.note: Standard employee slip; T4A for other income, T5 for investments. The Canadian version of the Italian CUD / CU.

ex.t: Your SIN starts with 9 if you're on a work permit.
ex.n: Il tuo SIN inizia con 9 se sei con permesso di lavoro.

items.note: Social Insurance Number. Required for employment and government services.

ex.t: The Notice of Assessment arrives two to eight weeks after filing.
ex.n: L'avviso di accertamento arriva in due-otto settimane dopo la trasmissione.

items.note: The CRA's formal response to your return, with the final numbers.

ex.t: A $437 refund — small, but mine.
ex.n: Un rimborso di 437 dollari — piccolo, ma mio.

items.note: Verb: to refund. Also simply: get back. Direct deposit: a 10-day refund.

ex.t: If you earn freelance income, you often have a balance owing.
ex.n: Se guadagni come freelance, hai spesso un saldo da pagare.

items.note: The opposite of a refund. CRA interest kicks in after April 30.

ex.t: RRSP contributions are a deduction.
ex.n: I contributi RRSP sono una detrazione.

items.note: Reduces taxable income. Different from a credit (reduces tax owed directly).

ex.t: The GST/HST credit is a quarterly payment for low-income earners.
ex.n: Il credito GST/HST è un pagamento trimestrale per redditi bassi.

items.note: Tax credit reduces tax directly. Refundable: pays even if you owe no tax. Non-refundable: only reduces to zero.

ex.t: RRSP contributions are deductible up to 18% of income.
ex.n: I contributi RRSP sono detraibili fino al 18% del reddito.

items.note: Registered Retirement Savings Plan. From unit 20.

ex.t: The TFSA contribution room for 2026: $7,000.
ex.n: Il tetto di contribuzione TFSA 2026: 7.000 dollari.

items.note: Tax-Free Savings Account. From unit 20.

ex.t: HST in Ontario: 13% (5% GST + 8% PST).
ex.n: HST in Ontario: 13% (5% GST + 8% PST).

items.note: Harmonized / Goods and Services Tax. From unit 20. GST/HST credit (payment to low-income earners) is different.

ex.t: An annual performance review is standard.
ex.n: Il colloquio annuale è lo standard.

items.note: Also appraisal. One-on-one feedback meeting with your manager.

ex.t: A 1.25-dollar-an-hour raise, effective March 15.
ex.n: Un aumento di 1,25 dollari all'ora dal 15 marzo.

items.note: Also pay rise (British). Ask for a raise: chiedere un aumento. Give someone a raise.

ex.t: A reference letter from Doug for the immigration file.
ex.n: Una lettera di raccomandazione da Doug per la pratica d'immigrazione.

items.note: Also recommendation letter, letter of support. Signed by the manager, on company letterhead.

ex.t: Six months of probation is standard in Ontario.
ex.n: Sei mesi di prova è lo standard in Ontario.

items.note: In Ontario, often three months by labour law and extended by contract.

ex.t: The Ontario minimum wage: $17.20 as of October 2025.
ex.n: Il salario minimo dell'Ontario: 17,20 dollari a ottobre 2025.

items.note: Reviewed annually. Student minimum, server minimum apply in some cases.

ex.t: The ESA sets minimum hours, vacation, and overtime.
ex.n: L'ESA stabilisce ore minime, ferie e straordinari.

items.note: Provincial law. Each province has its own equivalent.

ex.t: Vacation pay in Ontario: 4% of earnings for the first five years, 6% after.
ex.n: Ferie retribuite in Ontario: 4% dei guadagni per i primi cinque anni, 6% dopo.

items.note: Paid as salary and / or as time off. Usually 10 days a year up to year 5.

ex.t: In Ontario, 3 unpaid sick days a year, by law.
ex.n: In Ontario, 3 giorni di malattia non retribuiti all'anno, per legge.

items.note: ESA minimum. Many employers offer more. Compare: Italian system is much richer.

ex.t: Overtime starts after 44 hours a week in Ontario.
ex.n: Lo straordinario parte dopo le 44 ore settimanali in Ontario.

items.note: Overtime pay = 1.5 × regular rate.

ex.t: Statutory notice: 1 week per year of employment, max 8 weeks.
ex.n: Preavviso di legge: 1 settimana per anno, max 8 settimane.

items.note: Minimum from the ESA. Many contracts give more. In lieu of notice: paid instead.

ex.t: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing with regard to…
ex.n: Egregio Signore o Signora, Le scrivo in merito a…

items.note: When the recipient is unknown. Alternative: Dear + name (if known). «To whom it may concern» = a chi di competenza (very impersonal).

ex.t: I am writing with regard to the furnace outage.
ex.n: Le scrivo in merito al guasto della caldaia.

items.note: Formal register. Also concerning. Not «in regards to» (common error).

ex.t: I would be grateful if you could confirm this in writing.
ex.n: Le sarei grata se potesse confermarlo per iscritto.

items.note: + past tense (would be grateful if you could, not if you can). Formal courtesy.

ex.t: Please find attached the receipt and the T4.
ex.n: In allegato la ricevuta e il T4.

items.note: Also attached please find. Modern alternative: I attach / I am attaching.

ex.t: I am writing to request information about your winter courses.
ex.n: Le scrivo per chiedere informazioni sui vostri corsi invernali.

items.note: Opener of a formal letter. Compare informal: I'm writing to say / to let you know.

ex.t: Yours faithfully (if you don't know the recipient's name). Yours sincerely (if you do).
ex.n: Yours faithfully (destinatario sconosciuto). Yours sincerely (destinatario noto).

items.note: British English distinction, still used in formal Canadian correspondence. US: Sincerely yours or just Sincerely.

ex.t: Best regards, Chiara Russo.
ex.n: Cordiali saluti, Chiara Russo.

items.note: Modern business standard. Warmer than Yours faithfully.

items.t: it has come to my attention

ex.t: It has come to my attention that an error was made in my file.
ex.n: Sono venuta a conoscenza che un errore è stato fatto nella mia pratica.

items.note: Opener of a complaint. Impersonal, authoritative.

ex.t: In reference to your email of May 3rd…
ex.n: In riferimento alla sua email del 3 maggio…

items.note: Also «referring to», «as per your email».

ex.t: To Whom It May Concern: this letter confirms Chiara Russo's employment…
ex.n: A chi di competenza: la presente conferma l'impiego di Chiara Russo…

items.note: A very impersonal opener, for reference letters and general affidavits. Capitalise each word.

ex.t: Positive feedback and constructive criticism.
ex.n: Feedback positivo e critiche costruttive.

items.note: Uncountable. Give / provide / receive feedback. Also: give me a heads-up.

ex.t: Let's talk about your strengths and weaknesses this month.
ex.n: Parliamo dei tuoi punti forti e deboli questo mese.

items.note: Standard interview and review categories.

ex.t: Three areas for improvement next quarter.
ex.n: Tre aree di miglioramento per il prossimo trimestre.

items.note: The polite version of weaknesses. Standard HR language.

ex.t: Let's set goals for the second half of the year.
ex.n: Fissiamo obiettivi per la seconda metà dell'anno.

items.note: Goal, objective, target. SMART goals: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound.

ex.t: A promotion to assistant manager.
ex.n: Una promozione ad assistente responsabile.

items.note: Promote (verb): to promote someone. Opposite: a demotion.

ex.t: Her track record is excellent.
ex.n: Il suo andamento è eccellente.

items.note: The accumulated history of someone's performance.

ex.t: I appreciate your willingness to clean a floor at 7 a.m.
ex.n: Apprezzo la tua disponibilità a pulire un pavimento alle 7.

items.note: Willing to + inf. More formal than ready to.

ex.t: Her attention to detail has improved our Instagram.
ex.n: La sua attenzione ai dettagli ha migliorato il nostro Instagram.

items.note: A classic HR evaluation phrase.

ex.t: You report to me, I report to Doug.
ex.n: Tu riporti a me, io riporto a Doug.

items.note: In hierarchical sense; also report an incident to someone.

ex.t: The raise is effective from March 15.
ex.n: L'aumento ha decorrenza dal 15 marzo.

items.note: Also effective immediately. The formal date phrase for an administrative decision.

sections.title: Relative clauses, formal register, obligation modals
sections.intro: Three pieces: defining vs non-defining relative clauses (with the five relative pronouns), the formal English register, and the full set of obligation modals.

blocks.title: Relative clauses: defining and non-defining
blocks.rule: Relative clauses add information to a noun. Two types with different rules. Defining relative clause: identifies the noun; essential; no commas. Pronouns: who (people), which / that (things), whose (possession), where (place), when (time), or zero when the pronoun is the object. The volunteer who helped me was Prisca. The receipt that she gave me is in my file. The clinic where I filed is on College Street. The year when I filed. The receipt she gave me. Non-defining relative clause: adds extra info; dispensable; between commas. Pronouns: who, which, whose, where, when (never that). The clinic, which is on the Library's page, opens at 2 p.m. My T4, which Doug mailed, arrived on Thursday. Both types use whose for possession (whose attention) and where / when for place / time. In writing, use that in defining clauses and which in non-defining to make the distinction visually.

blocks.caption: Defining vs non-defining
head: Pattern
Defining (no comma)
Non-defining (with comma)
rows: The volunteer who helped me was great.
Prisca, who helped me, is a retired accountant.
The clinic which / that is on College Street.
The CVITP, which is a federal program, is free.
The slip that Doug sent me.
The baker whose pasticciotti sell out.
Doug, whose bakery I work at, is 72.
The office where I filed is downtown.
Toronto, where I live, is in Ontario.
The year when I came was 2024.
2024, when I came, was a snowy year.

blocks.title: Che vs that/which/who
blocks.text: Italian [[che]] does the work of English who/which/that for defining relatives. Italian [[il quale]] / [[la quale]] does the work of English who/which in non-defining (= with a comma). The English zero relative (the slip Doug sent me) has an Italian equivalent — the full [[che]] (il modulo che Doug ha mandato); Italian never omits the relative pronoun.

items.wrong: The volunteer, that helped me, was great.
items.right: The volunteer who helped me was great. OR The volunteer, who helped me, was great.
items.why: Defining uses who/that (no commas). Non-defining uses who/which (with commas), never that.

items.wrong: The CRA, that processes returns, is federal.
items.right: The CRA, which processes returns, is federal.

items.wrong: Prisca is the volunteer, which helped me.
items.right: Prisca is the volunteer who helped me. OR Prisca, who helped me, is a volunteer.
items.why: Who for people (not which); defining or non-defining decides the comma.

items.right: The office where I filed. OR The office at which I filed.
items.why: For place: where (or at which, formal). Not which alone.

blocks.title: Formal English
blocks.rule: The register of a formal English letter has fixed openings, closings, and connectors. Openings: Dear + title + name (Dear Dr. Smith); Dear Sir / Madam (recipient unknown); Dear Hiring Manager (role, if role is known); To Whom It May Concern (impersonal, reference letters). First paragraph: I am writing to… / I am writing with regard to… / I am writing in response to your email of… / I would like to apply for the position of… Phrases: with reference to / in reference to; please find attached / I attach / I enclose; I would be grateful if you could + base (not can); I look forward to hearing from you; your prompt attention to this matter would be appreciated; thank you for your consideration. Closings: Yours faithfully (if no name used in opening; British); Yours sincerely (if name used; British); Sincerely / Sincerely yours (US); Best regards / Kind regards / Regards (modern business). Nominalisations and passives are common: your prompt reply would be appreciated, in reference to the above matter, the matter has been investigated. Avoid contractions, slang, phrasal verbs (prefer discuss over talk about).

blocks.title: Modals of obligation: must / have to / need to / be required to / be supposed to
blocks.rule: The full set of English modals for obligation and expectation. Must + base: speaker's authority or strong rule. I must leave by nine. You must sign here. Negative mustn't = prohibition. Have to + base: external obligation (law, boss, situation). I have to work on Saturday. Negative don't have to = no need. Need to + base: necessity (practical). I need to practise my pronunciation. Negative don't need to = unnecessary. Be required to + base: formal, legal; passive-feeling. We are required to keep your records. Statutory obligation. Be supposed to + base: expected, but softer than must. You're supposed to track inventory. Negative aren't supposed to = you shouldn't. Should + base: advice, less than must. You should ask for a raise. Had better + base: a hint of warning. You'd better check that before signing. Past: had to (external past obligation), must have / had + part. (past deduction and past obligation, unit 20 recap). Was / were supposed to: did an expected thing not happen? You were supposed to call. The three modals (must, should, need to) and the semi-modals (have to, be required to, be supposed to, had better) overlap heavily; each carries a shade.

blocks.title: Italian equivalents
blocks.text: English must = Italian [[dovere]]; mustn't = [[non dovere]] / [[è vietato]]. Have to = Italian [[dovere]] (external). Need to = Italian [[avere bisogno di]] / [[dovere]]. Be required to = Italian [[essere tenuto a]] / [[dover]]. Be supposed to = Italian [[dovrebbe]] (ma non è detto) / [[si dovrebbe]]. All of them collapse into dovere in Italian, with context deciding the shade.

sections.title: The CRA, Service Canada, the pay slip
sections.intro: Four pages: the April 30 deadline, the CRA / Service Canada split, the Canadian pay slip, and employment-standards reality.

blocks.text: Canada's tax year is the calendar year. The deadline for most people to file their [[tax return]] (T1 General) is [[April 30]]. The self-employed can file by June 15, but any balance owing must still be paid by April 30. The [[CRA]] offers three ways to file: through a certified tax preparer; through a tax-filing software ([[TurboTax]], [[Wealthsimple Tax]], [[UFile]], [[H&R Block]] — several free for simple returns under a certain income); through the [[CRA My Account]] portal using [[NETFILE]] (direct submission to the CRA, standard for most individuals). The [[CVITP]] ([[Community Volunteer Income Tax Program]]) runs free clinics for low-income filers at libraries, community centres and places of worship from March to April. Volunteers are trained by the CRA, work in branded clinics, and submit returns through a special pathway. For a Toronto Working Holiday permit holder earning around 35,000 CAD, a tax clinic is the standard route. The [[Notice of Assessment]] (NOA) arrives two to eight weeks later with the final numbers and any refund or balance. Keep all documents for seven years; the CRA can audit back that far.

Two different federal departments. The [[CRA]] (Canada Revenue Agency, canada.ca/en/revenue-agency) is the tax authority. [[Service Canada]] (canada.ca/en/employment-social-development) is the social-service authority: it administers [[EI]] (Employment Insurance = unemployment and parental leave), [[CPP]] (Canada Pension Plan), [[OAS]] (Old Age Security), the [[SIN]], and [[passports]]. The [[provincial]] equivalents are [[ServiceOntario]], [[ServiceBC]], etc.: driver's licence, health card (OHIP), vehicle registration. Three different windows for three different problems. In practice, most interactions have moved online — CRA My Account for taxes, ESDC's My Service Canada Account for EI / CPP, ServiceOntario for most provincial needs. The paper-based office exists but is secondary. A newcomer typically visits [[Service Canada]] in the first month (for the SIN) and the [[CRA]] every April.

blocks.title: The Canadian pay slip
blocks.text: A Canadian pay slip (also called a [[pay stub]]) has the same information in every province: name, period, hours, gross pay, deductions (CPP, EI, income tax, union dues if any), and net pay. The three mandatory federal deductions: [[CPP]] (Canada Pension Plan): 5.95% of pensionable earnings; [[EI]] (Employment Insurance): 1.63% of insurable earnings; [[income tax]] (federal + provincial, progressive). Ontario progressive brackets 2026: 20.05% (first 51k), 24.15% (next 51k), 29.65% (next 60k), 31.48% (next 61k), 33.89% (over 220k) when federal + provincial are combined. A baker at Doug's earning $19.25 an hour, 40 hours a week, grosses around $40,000 a year, nets around $31,500 after deductions. Chiara's pay slip is similar. The December pay slip has the year-to-date totals that become the T4 in February.
The ESA, feedback and the performance review

Ontario's [[Employment Standards Act]] (ESA) sets the floor for private-sector workers (public sector follows other rules). The minimums as of October 2025: [[minimum wage]] $17.20; [[max weekly hours]] 48 before written agreement; [[overtime]] after 44 hours, at 1.5× rate; [[annual leave]] 2 weeks (4% pay) for first 5 years, 3 weeks (6%) after; [[public holidays]] 9 statutory; [[sick days]] 3 unpaid; [[termination notice]] 1 week per year up to 8 weeks, or pay in lieu; [[statutory holidays]] (New Year's, Family Day, Good Friday, Victoria Day, Canada Day, Civic / August long weekend, Labour Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, Boxing Day). Collective bargaining and good employers usually offer more. The [[performance review]] is a North American ritual: once or twice a year, often tied to a potential raise or promotion. The usual structure: strengths, areas for improvement, goals for next period, and sometimes a 360° feedback (peers also comment). Chiara's first review is a mild, well-run version with a direct offer of a raise and a letter of support.
